hypothesis: GET /api/auth/credential relies on get_verified_user_with_grace which does not compare the JWT version (payload.ver) against the database credential_version. When a user rotates credentials after an exploit or device loss, an attacker holding a pre-rotation token (ver < db_ver) can query /api/auth/credential and receive the newly rotated, decrypted recovery key, entirely bypassing key rotation.

When two legacy devices (holding the same historical UUID) reconnect concurrently and request POST /api/auth/session, both pass the recovery_key_id is None check and generate different keys. The second update overwrites the database without optimistic locking, leaving the first device with an unrecoverable ghost credential.

In-flight session promise deduplication is restricted to a single browser tab. Multiple tabs opening simultaneously issue concurrent /api/auth/session requests triggering 429 rate limits. Naively calling navigator.locks.request without feature detection crashes test environments (Vitest/jsdom) and non-secure contexts, and lacking timeout handling induces tab lock starvation.
